heroHeadline: China Coast Guard Rams Philippine BFAR Vessel Off Palawan; PCG Calls It 'Intentional Ramming'
heroSubtitle: China Coast Guard vessel CCG-21585 rammed the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources ship BRP Datu Magat Salamat on September 18, 2026, about 54 nautical miles off Palawan and 6.36 nautical miles north-northwest of Abad Santos Shoal, while the vessel was on a fuel subsidy mission to Filipino fishermen. PCG spokesperson Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela said the Chinese vessel cut across the BFAR ship's stern at 11:04 a.m. before striking it at 11:13 a.m., bending and detaching railings and deforming deck structures on the starboard side; no injuries were reported. China Coast Guard disputed the account, blaming the Philippine vessel for cutting across its bow. The National Task Force for the West Philippine Sea condemned the ramming as reckless. The incident came a day after the same vessel was refloated following a self-inflicted grounding at Hasa-Hasa (Half Moon) Shoal on September 17, and follows the AFP's September 15 assessment that the Haiyang Dizhi Shihao survey vessel's ~28-day presence off Bajo de Masinloc showed no confirmed drilling activity, amid a weekly tally of 48 Chinese vessels across four contested WPS features.
